one_liner: Small GPL C++ header (KISS + Marsaglia-Tsang Ziggurat) for standard normal, exponential, uniform draws; 4.7-7.4x faster than base R.
what_it_does: zigg is a CRAN package that exports zrnorm(n), zrexp(n), zrunif(n) and zsetseed(seed), which return vectors of N(0,1), Exp(1) and U(0,1) draws. The engine is a self-contained C++ header, inst/include/zigg/header, with class zigg::Ziggurat (rnorm(), rexp(), runi(), setSeed(), getPars()/setPars()) and no R dependency. Four demo packages show other packages calling it from C or C++ through registered C-callables or the header. It is its own generator (a 32-bit KISS core plus Ziggurat tables), not a distribution adaptor over a std:: URBG.
how_it_is_fast: It implements Marsaglia and Tsang's Ziggurat with the Leong et al. (2005) correction: a 128-strip table for the normal and a 256-strip table for the exponential, built once in the constructor. One 32-bit KISS draw (MWC xor CONG, plus SHR3) supplies both the strip index (low bits) and the candidate, so most draws cost one integer compare and one multiply; only strip edges and the tail call exp or log. Base R instead runs the Mersenne Twister and, for normals, inversion per draw, and runi() is a single scaled 32-bit integer.
when_to_use: R code where drawing millions of standard normals dominates run time: the author measured 7.4x over rnorm at 1e6 draws per call.
Native code in another R package that needs a fast N(0,1) generator without Rcpp, through R_GetCCallable or the header (four demo packages show the patterns).
Standalone C++11 code that wants a tiny, dependency-free Ziggurat normal generator and can accept GPL (>= 2) and a 32-bit KISS core.
Exploratory simulations with modest statistical demands, which is how the author frames it.
when_not_to_use: Exponential variates, unless you patch the table bug described under gotchas: as shipped, zrexp()/rexp() put about 8.7x too much mass beyond x = 7.697.

Results that must survive statistical scrutiny or match R's RNG streams: DESCRIPTION warns of 'potentially lesser quality and shorter period', the README recommends staying with base R when in doubt, and set.seed() does not control it (it has its own zsetseed()).
Proprietary or permissively licensed code: the header is GPL (>= 2).
Concurrent use: the R entry points share one static zigg::Ziggurat, and the object keeps scratch state (hz, iz, jz) in members.
Non-standard parameters or other distributions: there are no mean/sd/rate/min/max arguments, so you scale the output yourself; use Zest or dqrng for more distributions.

integration.dependencies: none for the header (C++ standard library only); R for the package
integration.platforms: any; portable 32-bit integer arithmetic, no SIMD
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. Generator state and per-call scratch (hz, iz, jz) live in the object and the R functions share one static instance, so use one object per thread from C++ and do not call the R functions concurrently.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — zrnorm(n)/zrexp(n)/zrunif(n) replace rnorm(n)/rexp(n)/runif(n) only at default parameters, are seeded by zsetseed() rather than set.seed(), and produce a different stream

gotchas: Correctness bug in the exponential table setup: 'ke[0] = (uint32_t) (de/q)*m2;' casts 0.885 to 0 before multiplying, so ke[0] = 0 instead of about 3.80e9 and every base-strip draw (1 in 256) goes to the tail sampler. A Python port of the header (1e6 draws) gave P(X > 7.697) = 0.00394 and mean 1.019, against 0.00045 and 1 for exact Exp(1); with the cast fixed it gave 0.00041 and 1.001. The same line is in RcppZiggurat's Ziggurat.h.

The constructor ignores its seed argument: unless ZIGG_USE_ORIGINAL_FIXED_INITIALIZATION is defined, it overwrites the seed with the current time in milliseconds, so call setSeed() after construction for reproducible runs. setSeed() only XORs the seed into the SHR3 word and resets the other three words to constants, which allows at most 2^32 seeded streams.
Draws have 32-bit resolution: runi() is 0.5 + int32(KISS) * 0.2328306e-09, and rnorm() uses one 32-bit draw for both the 7-bit strip index and the value.
The header #defines znew, wnew, MWC, SHR3 and CONG and #undefs them at the end, which clobbers any same-named macros in the including code.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: In R, dqrng reports a similar 7.6x on rnorm with xoshiro256++/PCG64 generators. Pick zigg only for its tiny zero-dependency C-callable interface. In C++, Zest (more distributions, any 32/64-bit URBG) or cxx-ziggurat and normaldist-benchmark pair the Ziggurat with a modern URBG; pick zigg only for a self-contained KISS + Ziggurat normal generator.
verified_claims_summary: inst/example/timings.R uses microbenchmark to time zrnorm/zrexp/zrunif against base R rnorm/rexp/runif at N = 1e6 draws per call. The README and DESCRIPTION report 7.4x, 5.2x and 4.7x 'on our machine', with no CPU, compiler, flags or R version. The baseline is R's built-in generators, not std:: <random>.
status_note: Recent commits only touch CI; the last package change is release 0.0.2 (2025-02-07, on CRAN, GPL >= 2). The header is small enough to vendor into GPL-compatible code, after fixing the ke[0] line.
